title: Got To Roll With The Punches
author: Brainard Carey

spans.text: Sometimes life can throw us curveballs. When things seem to be chugging along, progress happening, out of nowhere we get hit with an obstacle that knocks us down for bit. It happens to everybody at some time or another, and while it can be demoralizing to feel like you’ve been thrown off course, you can and will regain your footing. For artists, this can feel like a particularly existential threat, putting a hard built career in jeopardy. But there are always more opportunities out there, and even when you’re down and out, hope lingers on the horizon.

Brainard Carey is an author, artist and educator. He is the director of Praxis Center for Aesthetics and is currently faculty at the School of Visual Arts in NYC. He has written seven books for artists, including
Making it in the Art World
The Problems in the Art World: An Artist’s A-Z Action Guide

At times it can feel like everyone else is getting the exhibition, the grant, the residency, or the attention you’ve been working toward. Building an art career is rarely a straight line, rather it’s a process of showing up, continuing to make work that matters to you, and staying connected to opportunities that can move your practice forward. Every application you submit, every new resource you discover, and every connection you make adds another piece to the foundation you’re building.
